question: A rectangular coil is moving in a uniform magnetic field. The direction of the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of the coil. If the speed of the moving coil in the magnetic field decreases, then:

options.text: it will strengthen the magnetic field
it will destroy the magnetic field

solution:
The correct answer is __**induced potential difference decreases**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a rectangular coil is moving in a uniform magnetic field, and the speed of the coil decreases, the Induced potential difference decreases.
 
• **Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction** states that the induced electromotive force (EMF) in a closed loop is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux through the loop.
 
• The formula for induced EMF is given by :EMF = − d Φ B d t EMF=−dtdΦB​
 
• where ΦB\Phi_B ΦB​ is the magnetic flux.
 
• When the speed of the moving coil decreases, the rate at which the coil cuts through the magnetic field lines also decreases.
 
• This results in a reduction in the rate of change of magnetic flux through the coil. Consequently, the induced EMF (or potential difference) decreases as the speed of the coil slows down

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other options are incorrect because:
 
• The magnetic field itself is not strengthened or destroyed by the movement of the coil; it remains uniform unless externally changed.
 
• The potential difference does not increase as the speed decreases; rather, it is inversely related.
